lessons.title: The person who
lessons.scenario: At the campsite, Smarty and Ben talk about the guide and friends on their trip.

items.example: We need someone who knows this forest well.
items.note: Use 'someone who' when you talk about any person with a certain skill or quality.

items.example: A person who camps should always bring a torch.
items.note: Say 'a person who' to describe one type of person in general.

items.example: People who walk on trails must wear hiking boots.
items.note: Use 'people who' when talking about a group of people.

items.note: Use 'the man who' to identify a specific man by what he does or did.

items.example: Zara is a friend who loves sleeping in a tent.
items.note: Say 'a friend who' to describe one of your friends in more detail.

grammar.explanation: Use 'who' right after a person noun (someone, a person, people, the guide, the man, a friend) to explain which person you mean.

lessons.title: Things that
lessons.scenario: Smarty and Zara talk about useful camping gear and their favorite spots in the forest.

items.example: A torch is something that you need at night.
items.note: Use 'something that' to describe a thing by what it does or why it is useful.

items.example: The compass is the thing which helped us most.
items.note: Say 'the thing which' to point out one specific object.

items.example: A campsite is a place where people pitch tents.
items.note: Use 'a place where' to describe what happens at a location.

items.example: I still remember the day when we reached the summit.
items.note: Say 'the day when' to talk about an important day in a story or memory.

items.example: The rain was the reason why we stayed in the tent.
items.note: Use 'the reason why' to explain what caused something to happen.

items.example: My backpack is the one that is next to the tree.
items.note: Say 'the one that' to pick out one specific thing from several similar things.

grammar.title: Relative clauses with which, that, where, when, why
grammar.explanation: Use 'which' or 'that' for things (something that, the thing which, the one that), 'where' for places (a place where), 'when' for times (the day when), and 'why' for reasons (the reason why).
examples: A tent is something that keeps you dry.
This forest is a place where we love to camp.

grammar.title: Past ability and possibility
grammar.explanation: For one difficult success in the past, use 'was able to', 'managed to', or 'succeeded in' + -ing (do not use 'could' for a single hard achievement). For past inability, use 'was unable to' or 'were not able to'. For possibility, use 'might'.
examples: I managed to climb the steep path.
We succeeded in crossing the cold river.
We were not able to see the summit in the clouds.

episode.title: The Secret Trail in the Reserve

panels.speaker: Smarty
panels.text: The storm is over! Let us pack our backpacks and follow the trail to the summit.

image.describe: Smarty the black cat, Mia, and Sam standing outside their green tent in a sunny forest clearing with packed backpacks.

panels.speaker: Mia
panels.text: Look at my compass. There is a steep path behind that tall tree.

image.describe: Mia the cat holding an open pocket compass and pointing toward a narrow steep path between pine trees.

panels.speaker: Sam
panels.text: I brought drinking water, matches, and a first aid kit just in case!

image.describe: Sam the cat showing a water bottle and a small red first aid kit beside his backpack.

panels.speaker: Smarty
panels.text: All of a sudden, a red fox ran across the path and stopped near a small cave.

image.describe: A bright red fox pausing on a rocky mountain trail near a small dark cave entrance while Smarty watches.

panels.speaker: Mia
panels.text: To our surprise, there is an old metal box inside! Let me shine my torch on it.

image.describe: Mia shining a yellow torch beam into the cave onto an old metal box resting on the ground.

panels.speaker: Sam
panels.text: We managed to open it! Inside is a map that shows a secret lake in the mountains.

image.describe: Smarty, Mia, and Sam looking excitedly at an unfolded old paper map showing mountains and a blue lake.

panels.speaker: Smarty
panels.text: Omar is the guide who knows this nature reserve best. Let us show him at the campfire!

image.describe: Smarty holding the old map carefully while walking back toward the campsite with Mia and Sam.

panels.speaker: Omar
panels.text: This map leads to a place where no explorer has been for a hundred years! Are you ready for tomorrow?

image.describe: Omar the ranger cat examining the map by the glowing campfire as Smarty, Mia, and Sam smile with excitement under the stars.
